summary: Deep module. Discovery-Login without CHAP is T1; Normal-session Login to FullFeaturePhase + INQUIRY/READ CAPACITY on LUN 0 is T2 proof-of-exploit (real block-device access, read-only). Missing T3 loot: pull a raw sector to file (dd) and pull VMDK/partclone dump.

findings.tier_evidence: Login handshake completion is fingerprint only.

findings.title_pattern: iSCSI target - AuthMethod=None accepted for Discovery session
findings.tier_evidence: Deterministic: AuthMethod=None + StatusClass=0 on a Discovery Login only if target explicitly permits it. No exploit payload.
findings.promotion_notes: Already promoted via _emit_auth_none_normal + INQUIRY/READ CAPACITY, but this specific finding stops at T1.
findings.tester_next_step: iscsiadm -m discovery -t sendtargets -p IP:3260  # captures every TargetName/TargetAddress

findings.title_pattern: unauthenticated SendTargets discloses all IQNs and portal addresses
findings.tier_evidence: SendTargets=All succeeds only when unauth Discovery Login was accepted; the target list itself proves the exposure.
findings.promotion_notes: For each disclosed IQN, run a Normal Login attempt on its portal — the module already does this for the first target; extending to all N would raise coverage.
findings.tester_next_step: for iqn in $(iscsiadm -m discovery -t sendtargets -p IP:3260 | awk '{print $2}'); do iscsiadm -m node -T $iqn -p IP:3260 --login; done

findings.title_pattern: iSCSI target - AuthMethod=None accepted for Normal session (raw LUN mount, no credential)
findings.tier_evidence: Reaching FullFeaturePhase on a Normal session with AuthMethod=None is real access to the LUN plane, verified by follow-on INQUIRY. Recce did not write data — proof of exploit without full compromise.
findings.promotion_notes: Automate iscsiadm login + `dd if=/dev/sdX bs=1M count=1 of=lun-sample.bin` to prove first-block extraction; hash-match to LUKS/VMDK/ext4 magic like nbd does. New: session-kill after sample.
findings.tester_next_step: modprobe iscsi_tcp; iscsiadm -m node -T <iqn> -p IP:3260 --login; ls /dev/disk/by-path/*iscsi*; dd if=/dev/sdX bs=1M count=64 of=/tmp/lun0.img; file /tmp/lun0.img

findings.title_pattern: iSCSI target - INQUIRY leaks LUN vendor / product / revision
findings.tier_evidence: SCSI INQUIRY on LUN 0 succeeds ONLY when a Normal session reached FullFeaturePhase — real SCSI command trip through the array.
findings.promotion_notes: Combined with iSCSI login + partclone dump, this becomes T3 credential pull off the block device.

findings.title_pattern: iSCSI target - READ CAPACITY (10) succeeded on LUN 0 (LUN masking absent)
findings.tier_evidence: READ CAPACITY response returns real block count and size only after real block-device access — proves LUN masking is absent, does not exfiltrate any content.
findings.promotion_notes: Extend with a bounded READ(10) of block 0 and match magic like nbd_ndmp — mounts the volume without needing kernel iscsi_tcp.
findings.tester_next_step: sg_readcap /dev/disk/by-path/...-lun-0 ; then dd if=/dev/sdX of=lun0.raw bs=1M count=1 ; file lun0.raw

findings.title_pattern: iSCSI CHAP - challenge captured for offline cracking (hashcat -m 4800)
findings.tier_evidence: CHAP_I/CHAP_C returned is a real, freshly generated credential material — with an intercepted initiator response it is a T4 crack primitive. Without response it's more T1, but capture-formatted hashcat -m 4800 line is a proof artifact.
findings.promotion_notes: Currently the response side (CHAP_N + CHAP_R) is not captured. If recce can also observe/relay a real initiator (packet capture or a spoofed target listener), the pair becomes a full T4 crack loop.

findings.tier_evidence: Posture bit (mutual CHAP not demanded) — not a probe result.
findings.promotion_notes: Posture flag; promotion would require a live relay.
findings.tester_next_step: iscsiadm -m node -T <iqn> -p IP:3260 -o show | grep -i chap
iscsiadm -m node -T <iqn> -p IP:3260 -o show | grep -i digest

findings.title_pattern: SendTargets discloses internal-only storage-network portal IPs
findings.tier_evidence: Recon: portal IPs outside scan scope.
findings.promotion_notes: Try a Discovery Login against each pivoted portal IP to see whether unauth Discovery reaches internal-only segments; recce already has the code.
